# launch_game_json

[← Command index](README.md)

Launch a game described by its JSON file, installing it and restoring its save first.

## Synopsis

```
launch_game_json [options]
```

## Description

The game is given as a JSON file with `-i`, or by `-c`, `-s` and `-n`, which name the
JSON file under the `Roms` supercategory of the metadata repository; the `launch:` lines
in the Pegasus metadata files use this second form. With `-r`, whatever is not given
is picked at random, ending with a random game from that subcategory's metadata file.

Games whose metadata does not mark them playable are refused. A store game is
installed and started through its store, with its save imported before and exported
after. Any other game is installed into the local cache if needed, its save is imported
and linked into the emulator's save folder, the emulator's config file has its path
placeholders filled in, and the emulator is run; afterwards the config is restored and
the save exported.

Errors are shown as a popup and end the run.

## Options

### Game

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Game JSON file to launch; takes priority over `-c`, `-s` and `-n`. |
| `-l, --locker_type <locker_type>` | Locker type passed to the install step. Default: `Hetzner`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-c, --game_category <game_category>` | Category of the game, used with `-s` and `-n` to find its JSON file. Allowed: `Computer`, `Microsoft`, `Nintendo`, `Other`, `Sony`. |
| `-s, --game_subcategory <game_subcategory>` | Subcategory (platform) of the game, used with `-c` and `-n` to find its JSON file. Allowed: `Amazon Games`, `Disc`, `Epic Games`, `GOG`, `Humble Bundle`, `Itchio`, `Legacy Games`, `Puppet Combo`, `Red Candle`, `Square Enix`, `Steam`, `Zoom`, `Microsoft MSX`, `Microsoft Xbox`, `Microsoft Xbox 360`, `Microsoft Xbox 360 GOD`, `Microsoft Xbox 360 XBLA`, `Microsoft Xbox 360 XIG`, `Microsoft Xbox One`, `Microsoft Xbox One GOD`, `Nintendo 3DS`, `Nintendo 3DS Apps`, `Nintendo 3DS eShop`, `Nintendo 64`, `Nintendo Amiibo`, `Nintendo DS`, `Nintendo DSi`, `Nintendo Famicom`, `Nintendo Game Boy`, `Nintendo Game Boy Advance`, `Nintendo Game Boy Advance e-Reader`, `Nintendo Game Boy Color`, `Nintendo Gamecube`, `Nintendo NES`, `Nintendo SNES`, `Nintendo SNES MSU-1`, `Nintendo Super Famicom`, `Nintendo Super Game Boy`, `Nintendo Super Game Boy Color`, `Nintendo Switch`, `Nintendo Switch eShop`, `Nintendo Virtual Boy`, `Nintendo Wii`, `Nintendo Wii U`, `Nintendo Wii U eShop`, `Nintendo WiiWare`, `Apple iOS`, `Apple MacOS 8`, `Arcade`, `Atari 800`, `Atari 2600`, `Atari 5200`, `Atari 7800`, `Atari Jaguar`, `Atari Jaguar CD`, `Atari Lynx`, `Bandai WonderSwan`, `Bandai WonderSwan Color`, `Coleco ColecoVision`, `Commodore 64`, `Commodore Amiga`, `Google Android`, `Magnavox Odyssey 2`, `Mattel Intellivision`, `NEC PC-Engine`, `NEC PC-Engine CD`, `NEC SuperGrafx`, `NEC TurboGrafx-16`, `NEC TurboGrafx CD`, `Nokia N-Gage`, `Panasonic 3DO`, `Philips CDi`, `SNK Neo Geo Pocket Color`, `Sega 32X`, `Sega CD`, `Sega CD 32X`, `Sega Dreamcast`, `Sega Game Gear`, `Sega Genesis`, `Sega Master System`, `Sega Saturn`, `Sinclair ZX Spectrum`, `Texas Instruments TI-99-4A`, `Tiger Game.com`, `Sony PlayStation`, `Sony PlayStation 2`, `Sony PlayStation 3`, `Sony PlayStation 4`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation 3`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation 4`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable Minis`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Vita`, `Sony PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Portable Video`, `Sony PlayStation Vita`. |
| `-n, --game_name <game_name>` | Name of the game, used with `-c` and `-s` to find its JSON file. |
| `-r, --fill_with_random` | When `-i` or the full `-c`/`-s`/`-n` set is not given, pick the missing category, subcategory and game at random. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-t, --capture_type <Screenshot\|Video>` | Capture screenshots or a video while an emulated game runs; no capture when omitted. Allowed: `Screenshot`, `Video`. |
| `-f, --fullscreen` | Ask the emulator to run fullscreen. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Launch a game by name

```bash
launch_game_json -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo 64" -n "Game Name (USA)"
```

### Launch a game from its JSON file, fullscreen

```bash
launch_game_json -i "/path/to/Game Name (USA).json" -f
```

### Launch a random Nintendo game

```bash
launch_game_json -c Nintendo -r
```

### Launch and record a video of the session

```bash
launch_game_json -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo 64" -n "Game Name (USA)" -t Video
```

### Dry run

```bash
launch_game_json -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo 64" -n "Game Name (USA)" -p -v
```

## Notes

- Capture length, interval, area and frame rate come from the `[UserData.Capture]` section of JoyBox.ini.
- Random selection skips subcategories whose platform has no launcher.
